title: LEB — the structured findings of a delivery, next series
description: The index a delivery of the next series brings with its REPORT.md, as protocol/tasks/TASK-D-1.0.0.md §5 asks: the English counterpart of achados.schema.json, which the full LEB keeps. It feeds the matching of the report against the matrix. Validating it scores nothing and charges nothing: a delivery without it is evaluated the same way, at more work for the judge.

leb.description: Copied from the header of the TASK.md delivered. A mismatch means the delivery was made against another version of the instance, and the run is not comparable.

findings.description: One item per problem reported. No minimum or maximum count: the standard never reveals how many flaws exist.

not_changed.description: Explicit decisions not to change something. They feed the EXPL rubric (trade-offs).

id.description: The model's own identifier (F1, F2, …), unique in the file and the same as in REPORT.md. NOT a taxonomy id.

file.description: Path relative to the package, as delivered (e.g. code/src/...).

line.description: Line in the original numbering of the file received. Matches the matrix within ±10 lines or by the same function (MATRIX.md §5.2).

category.description: The neutral vocabulary of the task statement. The judge maps it to the taxonomy: architecture→ARCH, bug→BUG, performance→PERF, quality→CLN; other is anything else, judged as an extra finding.

confidence.description: 0–100: the declared probability that the problem is real. It feeds the Brier score; it is not part of the 1000 points.

mechanism.description: Why it fails, concretely, in this code. This is what the judge scores in C2/R2: generic text does not count.

fixed.description: The model's own statement. The mechanical evidence of the verifiers prevails over it.
